evidence.note: marshalCanonical unconditionally rewrites the six bytes \ufffd to a raw U+FFFD; reproduced with a scratch test that Canonical() then emits invalid JSON.
Canonical() routes every event payload through marshalCanonical, so the rewrite reaches every audit line.

Escape coverage exercises raw U+FFFD and \xff but never a literal backslash followed by ufffd, which is why the defect ships green.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/types.go:356 corrupts the audit chain. marshalCanonical ends with bytes.ReplaceAll(out, []byte(`\ufffd`), []byte("\ufffd")), rewriting the literal six-byte sequence backslash-u-f-f-f-d anywhere in the encoded output. That sequence also occurs as the tail of a legitimately escaped backslash: a payload string containing the text `\ufffd` encodes as `\\ufffd`, and the replacement matches at offset 1, yielding a lone backslash followed by a raw U+FFFD rune. That is not a valid JSON escape. Reproduced: Canonical(`{"issue_text":"the JSON escape \\ufffd is emitted"}`) returns bytes for which json.Valid is false, so Canonical violates its own documented contract (canonical.go:15-17: 'valid JSON ... Canonical is idempotent'). Because Canonical output is what Append writes and LineHash hashes, one such payload — trivially reachable, since findings/node_output/stderr carry arbitrary reviewer and diff text, and this very branch's docs discuss \ufffd — writes an undecodable line into the run log. parseLines (store.go:105) then rejects the entire run with ERR_AUDIT_CHAIN 'undecodable' on every subsequent read, and RepairTail only handles an unterminated tail, not a bad interior line, so the run is unrecoverable. Compounding it: the replacement is dead for its stated purpose on the toolchain in use — go1.27's encoder already writes invalid UTF-8 as a raw three-byte U+FFFD (verified), so the branch only ever fires on false positives.

findings.note: The U+FFFD arm of marshalCanonical is untested. canonical_test.go's toolchain-independence table covers U+2028/U+2029 only, and the escape round-trip list at canonical_test.go:134 uses a raw replacement char and a raw \xff byte — neither of which reaches the replacement. No test feeds a literal backslash-ufffd, so the corruption above is invisible to the suite. Any fix should land with that case pinned.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/types.go:364 double-quotes the run id: fmt.Errorf("invalid run id %q", strconv.Quote(id)) applies %q to an already-quoted string, so a bad id renders as invalid run id "\"foo\"". Either drop strconv.Quote or use %s.

internal/fsm/run/store.go:188 hardcodes DefaultMaxEvents in prepareCreate instead of the store's configured Options.MaxEvents, unlike Append (store_mem.go:74, store_jsonl.go:231, which pass s.opts.maxEvents()). Benign today because TypeInit is not a counted type, so the cap can never fire at seq 1 — but it is a silent divergence from the MaxEvents() contract documented at store.go:68 and will bite if the init envelope ever becomes counted.

internal/fsm/run/store.go:155-161 recomputes the counted-event total by json.Unmarshal-probing every previously stored line on each counted append. Combined with the jsonl store re-reading the whole audit file per append, appending N events is O(N^2) in both bytes and JSON parses; at the DefaultMaxEvents ceiling of 100,000 that is on the order of 5e9 line probes for one run. A counted-event tally carried in FoldState would make it O(1).

findings.note: internal/fsm/gate/gate_test.go:390 does not restore TMPDIR as intended. Line 386 sets TMPDIR to a non-existent directory; line 390's t.Setenv("TMPDIR", os.TempDir()) reads os.TempDir(), which on unix returns $TMPDIR — the bogus path just set — so it re-sets the broken value rather than restoring the original. Harmless only because t.Setenv unwinds at test end; capture os.TempDir() before line 386 (or drop line 390 and rely on t.Setenv's own restore) so the intent matches the behaviour.
